# Chip origins and differences between WASM and Native backends

This document describes the initial source snapshot inspected on 2026-10-24 and the subsequent component additions recorded below. The **reference Web implementation** is the Browser / WASM side of `hello_ymfm`; the **reference Native implementation** is the Tauri project `tetorica-fm2612-playground-tauri`. Upstream chip projects, those applications and this distributable SDK are separate layers.

## Comparison layers

1. **Upstream → Tetorica:** existing standalone adaptations, observation, muting, live edits and other changes. A core may already differ from its upstream source.
2. **Reference applications → SDK:** changes made while importing sources for distribution. Origins, versions and original / packaged hashes identify each snapshot.
3. **WASM ↔ Native:** shared cores can still have different rate conversion, Stop behavior, sample memory, output settings and APIs.

This SDK collects implementations already developed and checked in the reference applications, retaining their differences. Maintaining the collection does not require replacing every variant with one common version.

The original C/C++ and WASM import commit is `0fff93d46ab3e9227ecffcacdf96f3ca115e6f72`. The JavaScript ADPCM references were imported separately from `a9f9a8a86ec4bd182224b1bc3979cfde6cf95b48`. [source_inventory.json](../catalog/source_inventory.json) records each component's source version; it and [Native SOURCES.json](../native/reference/SOURCES.json) identify the exact included bytes by hash.

## Shared integration considerations

- WASM `*_generate` functions provide low-level block generation. Many Native wrappers convert to the device output rate, return a stereo frame through `*_sample`, and retain state for Stop, manual audition and individual source cancellation.
- Native `get_state` / snapshots do not advance audio or consume sample data. Some include status reads with flag/IRQ propagation, as documented for Y8950 below. A chip's opaque WASM save / load format is not necessarily interchangeable with a Native snapshot. Follow each header's contract.
- Native source cancellation is called by host ownership management. The SDK does not include the Tauri Rust queue, voice leases, copy-on-write memory lifetimes, 16-device / 64 MiB budgets, retirement or CPAL integration.
- The reference JavaScript Synth, AudioWorklet, Keyboard, sample editor, Mixer defaults, master volume and FX are outside this SDK. Applications must configure their own mixing and output levels.
- The standalone Native CMake targets cover **YM2612/YM2151/YM2413/YM2203/YM2608/YM2610/YM2610B and YM3526/YM3812/YMF262/Y8950 using ymfm, plus Sega PSG, AY-3-8910, OKIM6258, RF5C164, Game Boy, HuC6280, NES with optional FDS, 32X PWM, MSFA DX7, SNES S-DSP, SPC700/S-DSP playback and WonderSwan**: twenty-three chip IDs, plus alternative Nuked YM2612, in twenty static libraries. The alternative engine adds no chip identifier; separate Analyzer-only chip references remain outside the standalone target set. Included WASM recipes, completed SDK builds and platform results are recorded separately in [verification.md](verification.md).

## Native / WASM differences for the 23 public chip IDs

These differences mainly originate in the reference applications. Importing the sources into this SDK did not create them. Native links point to the included reference code.

| Public ID | Core and WASM interface | Native differences and integration requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ym2612` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opn.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2612_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2612.cpp) adds output-rate averaging / hold, an authored-register shadow, separate FM / CSM cancellation, DAC retention and deferred audition. A standalone Native target is provided. See Nuked below |
| `ym2203` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opn.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2203_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2203.cpp) handles the prescaler, retained SSG levels, Stop / CSM, audition at FM clock boundaries and output-rate conversion. The standalone `tetorica::ym2203` target exposes three FM and three SSG voices, including shared noise/envelope and synchronous read/status/IRQ/state observations. Both paths send combined mono FM+SSG to left and right. `native_ym2203_create()` retains output-rate remainder/held PCM across reset; `create_extra()` clears both, matching the additional Worklet profile. At the standard prescaler the SSG effective clock is master/2; unlike YM2608, tone frequency is master/(32*period). This target provides no YM2608 rhythm or ADPCM resources |
| `ym2608` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opn.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2608_wasm.cpp) | The standalone `tetorica::ym2608` target retains the [Native adapter](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2608.cpp): six FM, three SSG, six fixed-address rhythm voices and ADPCM-B, with preallocated 8 KiB ROM / 2 MiB RAM and synchronous bounded copies. The WASM ROM vector grows on load; its RAM is 2 MiB. Both Native profiles retain memory on Stop/reset. Primary reset clears outer held PCM/remainder; `create_extra()` retains it, opposite to YM2203. Additional cancellation retains separate held buses. `get_state()` / `get_extra_state()` are observational, whereas raw ADPCM CPU-data reads and extended-status IRQ propagation have side effects. Hosts supply encoded data, serialized access and event timing. The example's generated rhythm bytes are not a hardware ROM |
| `ym2610` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opn.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2610b_wasm.cpp) | The standalone shared [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2610b.cpp) selects immutable variant 0, FM mask `0x36` (physical slots 1/2/4/5), plus SSG and programmable ADPCM-A/B. Primary handles own two dense 16 MiB ROM banks with bounded synchronous copies. Additional handles borrow immutable 64 KiB pages across the same address spaces; nonempty `load_rom()` is rejected. Hosts own publication, lifetime/retirement and synchronization. Both reset profiles clear outer held PCM/remainder, retaining ROM bytes/page mappings, clock and source mute. Both status reads and snapshots are observational, unlike OPNA's extended-status propagation |
| `ym2610b` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opn.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2610b_wasm.cpp) | The same library exposes immutable six-FM variant 1, mask `0x3f`, with the same primary/additional memory contracts. `tetorica::ym2610b` and `<tetorica/ym2610b.hpp>` still require an explicit constructor variant; they do not select it automatically. WASM `ym2610b_create()` defaults to six FM channels, while Native `create_extra()` defaults to four. Use `create(rate, variant)` or `create_extra_variant(rate, variant)` explicitly. The aliases share one static library and preserve `native_ym2610b_*` rather than introducing a second ABI |
| `ym2151` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opm.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2151_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2151.cpp) adds per-source cached output / mute / CSM release, averaging / hold, audition and Stop. The standalone `tetorica::ym2151` target exposes eight FM channels, pan, timers/status/IRQ and observational state through the existing C ABI. It is OPM only; the separate OKIM6258 target can be combined by a host, as the offline X68000 example demonstrates |
| `ym2413` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opl.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym2413_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ym2413.cpp) retains separate cached output and cancellation for nine FM channels and rhythm aliases, power-on snapshot reset and held output during manual release. These operations have more specific semantics than a global key-off. The standalone `tetorica::ym2413` target provides nine melodic channels or six FM plus five logical drum voices sharing physical channels 6–8, with mono output on both stereo channels. Hosts can combine this FM component with the separate AY target for an MSX sound configuration; machine integration remains with the host |
| `ay8910` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-ay8910/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/ay8910_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_ay8910.cpp) uses a 1,789,773 Hz reference with outer clock averaging/hold, per-channel held output, retained levels, audition and remixing on forced off. The standalone `tetorica::ay8910` target preserves this adapter and its synchronous observation API. It fixes AY type 0 / flags 1 and averages three channel outputs, copying mono to both stereo channels. Its ABI does not expose raw WASM's YM2149/type/flags selection or a motherboard analog mixer |
| `ym3526` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opl.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym3526_wasm.cpp) | Kind 0 of standalone [primary OPL](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_opl.cpp) / [additional OPL](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_extra_opl.cpp): nine mono FM channels and shared rhythm. Both constructors require the kind explicitly even through `<tetorica/ym3526.hpp>`. Additional ordinary all-notes-off, host silencing, strong Stop/CSM cancellation and source-preview held timing remain separate operations |
| `ym3812` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opl.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ym3812_wasm.cpp) | Kind 1 in the same shared standalone library, with OPL2 waveform selection. Native wrappers retain authored registers, distinct primary/additional Stop/reset, held cancellation, audition, CSM and rate conversion. These host policies are more specific than the raw WASM register interface; the aliases do not change them |
| `y8950` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opl.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/y8950_wasm.cpp) | Kind 3 in the shared standalone library, FM plus mono ADPCM-B. WASM owns a vector up to 2 MiB; Native borrows [512 writable 4 KiB pages plus logical length/revisions](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_y8950_memory.h). CPU writes modify mapped bytes and increment memory revision; publishing length sets upload revision to the newly incremented memory revision. Stop/reset retain pages/metadata; destruction does not free them. Hosts own serialization and retirement, without the reference Rust COW manager/queues/budgets. Snapshots do not consume data or advance PCM, but Y8950 status inspection can propagate ADPCM flags into IRQ; raw CPU data reads have transfer side effects |
| `ymf262` | [ymfm](../vendor/ymfm/ymfm_opl.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/ymf262_wasm.cpp) | Kind 2 in the shared standalone library. Both paths fold A+C / B+D into stereo. The [additional Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_extra_opl.cpp) retains NEW mode authored/effective views, physical four-operator pairs and source cancellation without advancing foreign voices. Primary reset uses core reset; additional reset restores the captured power-on state and clears cached history. Preview and runtime release semantics remain distinct |
| `segapsg` | [Tetorica SegaPSG](../vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/segapsg.cpp) / [WASM](../wasm/segapsg_wasm.cpp) | [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_psg.h) adds outer averaging / hold at a retained reference clock, level retention and Stop; mute / stereo connect to the shared core. The standalone `tetorica::segapsg` target uses the independent Game Gear wrapper and keeps its `native_game_gear_*` ABI. Stereo `0xff` retains Genesis/Master System mono output on both channels; optional masks provide Game Gear routing. No OPLL core is included. The core now lives separately under `vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/` with its own BSD license and [SMS Power! hardware-documentation credit](../vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/README.md). It remains a Tetorica addition absent from the historical ymfm comparison below; `vendor/ymfm/chip_state.h` is only a shared Tetorica serialization dependency |
| `gameboy` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-gameboy/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/gameboy_apu_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::gameboy` preserves the [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_gameboy.cpp): internal 4,194,304 Hz reference, outer clock conversion, two pulses, owned 16-byte wave RAM, noise, gate-only Stop and observation. NR51 high/low nibbles route left/right; the retained NR50 interpretation uses low bits for left gain and high bits for right. Per-channel Stop clears core contributions but can retain an outer mixed sample below the reference clock until the next source frame; global Stop clears outer PCM immediately. Reset powers off and restores the DMG wave startup pattern, retaining clock/mute. The access-only friend amendment below enables the unchanged wrapper; it does not alter synthesis or add hardware readback |
| `nes` | [JSNES/fixNES port](../vendor/tetorica-nes/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/nesapu_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::nes` compiles the self-contained [Native renderer](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_nes.cpp), with immutable constructor base clock (NTSC/PAL threshold 1.7 MHz) and optional FDS flag. Both pulses, triangle/noise/DMC mix nonlinearly to mono; FDS adds its low-pass/DC-filtered wave, followed by the Native 10 Hz DC remover. Loads copy into owned 64 KiB RAM; reset clears it and FDS wave/modulation tables, retaining mute/current clock/FDS selection. Stop retains memory, DAC/filter history and outer held PCM; global Stop obeys FDS I/O, whereas `stop_channel(5)` halts despite disabled I/O. Source mute advances synthesis; state/memory/active reads do not advance or acknowledge IRQ. The two core sources differ only in their include name; WASM adds block generation and compiled state-layout descriptors. The 400-byte snapshot is observational, not a resumable save-state. The vendor implementation exports duplicate symbols and must not be linked alongside Native; neither core is modified |
| `snes` | [SNES-SPC](../vendor/snes-spc/README.md) / [shared WASM wrapper](../wasm/spc_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::snes` / `<tetorica/snes.hpp>` links the unchanged [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_snes.cpp) wrapper and accurate DSP only. Owns 64 KiB RAM; bounded uploads copy, while a read-only view remains valid until destruction with mutation excluded. Stereo 32 kHz synthesis is interpolated to 8–384 kHz output; there is no clock setter or SPC700. Same-frame KON / KOFF protection, retained Stop and reset are preserved. Stop resets active gates/history but retains RAM/settings, including potentially audible echo contents; reset clears RAM. [Timeline RAM / DSP / events](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_snes.h) remain borrowed immutable validated arrays through pause/end, until reset/global Stop/reprepare/destruction. The host supplies event validation, lifetime and serialization; four-frame initial delay/sub-frame event ordering are retained. See the [Native guide](../native/README.md#embed-snes-s-dsp); retain LGPL-2.1-or-later notices |
| `spc` | [SNES-SPC](../vendor/snes-spc/README.md) / [shared WASM wrapper](../wasm/spc_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::spc` / `<tetorica/spc.hpp>` retains the unchanged [Native](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_spc.cpp) SPC700 + accurate S-DSP player with fixed 32 kHz synthesis, 128-frame blocks and 8–384 kHz output interpolation. File loading copies state, but hosts retain original bytes for rewind/absolute-seek reconstruction. Load/seek/create/destroy belong on control before installing a handle; seek advances at most 16,000 native frames per call on a paused, non-observing player. Pause freezes without rewinding; mute can retain prefetched PCM/echo. Failed control operations latch errors until successful reload. Snapshots are analysis workspaces, not full save states; events borrow handle-owned storage with bounded capacity/overflow. The host supplies publication/retirement and serialized draining. It does not expose every WASM analysis API, such as trace / RAM discovery, or supply a full IPL/metadata-based ending. See the [Native SPC guide](../native/README.md#embed-spc700-file-playback); retain LGPL-2.1-or-later notices |
| `huc6280` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-huc6280/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/huc6280_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::huc6280` preserves the [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_huc6280.cpp), its 3,579,545 Hz reference and outer clock averaging/hold. Six audible channels own 32-sample unsigned 5-bit wave RAM/DDA; channels 4/5 add noise, and channel 1 supplies LFO to channel 0. Wave uploads copy immediately and preserve selection/control/DDA while resetting index and potentially retriggering phase. Explicit-channel writes restore selection; invalid channel arguments fall back to current selection. Mute preserves progression. Key-off/Stop clear enable bits but retain DDA mode/latches and outer held PCM; reset clears wave/register/output phase while retaining mute/clock. Creation guards 8–384 kHz; clock edits guard 100 kHz–100 MHz. State is observational. The wrapper uses private access and directly includes the vendor `.cpp`; CMake compiles no duplicate core translation unit. Native and WASM keep their distinct helper/API behavior |
| `rf5c164` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-rf5c164/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/rf5c164_wasm.cpp) | `tetorica::rf5c164` exposes both [primary](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_rf5c164.cpp) and [additional](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_extra_rf5c164.cpp) ABIs: eight voices, owned/copied 64 KiB RAM, reset retaining memory and a separate clear. Primary uses the vendor core with outer averaging/hold at a 12.5 MHz reference; extra is an independent implementation preserving reference bus PCM while tracking per-voice held contributions. Ordinary mask writes keep held-output timing; extra key-off/Stop remixes immediately without advancing foreign voices. CPU memory writes use bank OR offset, whereas bulk loads use absolute bounds. Primary accepts any nonzero rate, has a void unbounded clock setter and requires valid upload storage; extra guards 8–384 kHz / 100 kHz–100 MHz and rejects nonempty null uploads. Extra alone exposes state/readback and scoped cancellation. The profiles are not interchangeable thin wrappers |
| `okim6258` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-okim6258/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/okim6258_wasm.cpp) | `tetorica::okim6258` preserves the [Native additional-instance adapter](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_extra_okim6258.cpp): default 8 MHz/divider 512/flags 12, low-nibble-first 4-bit ADPCM with fixed 12-bit output, a sample feeder and repeat. It borrows up to 16 MiB of immutable bytes without copying; callers retain them across Stop/reset until replacement/destruction and serialize access/retirement. This differs from the X68000 primary path's two sample staging banks. Stop clears held output; reset restores divider 512/pan 0 and decoder phase while retaining clock/sample binding. Raw register hosts feed the bounded FIFO; convenience playback feeds the borrowed sample. No Native format selector, 3-bit ADPCM or recording is added |
| `pwm` | [32X extraction](../vendor/mame-32x-pwm/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/pwm32x_wasm.cpp) | Standalone `tetorica::pwm` preserves the [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_pwm.cpp), its `native_pwm_*` ABI and shared header-only core: 23,011,361 Hz / gain 1 / duty mode. The reference standalone JavaScript defaults to DAC mode / gain 0.4; its VGM comparison uses duty / 1. Native owns two three-entry FIFOs and latches, accepts 1–1,000,000 Hz output and 100 kHz–100 MHz clock edits, and integrates held duty over each output frame. The interval is cycle minus one clocks; duty neutral is cycle/2, while valid raw zero is -1. FIFO values copy immediately, with no borrowed sample storage. Nonzero 64-bit tags track queued/latched ownership only: scoped cancellation compacts matching entries and invalidates matching latches without advancing the timer or foreign state. Tag zero remains ordinary/unowned. Stop immediately empties queues/invalidates latches/clears tags while retaining routing/cycle/clock/timer/count history; reset clears chip/timer state and tags while retaining clock. Snapshots omit tags and are observational, not save/load. The SDK imports no scheduler, SH2, DMA or analog filter; the original 32X WAV example links separate FM/PSG handles. See the [Native guide](../native/README.md#embed-32x-pwm) for routing, overflow and active-write behavior |
| `dx7` | [Shared MSFA core](../vendor/msfa/UPSTREAM.md) / [WASM](../wasm/dx7/dx7.cc) | Standalone `tetorica::dx7` uses the unchanged [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_dx7.cpp) with exactly six shared-core overrides. Voices copy 155 unpacked bytes; matching identities scope live edits. Note On returns slots 0–15; masks can preserve released tails. Release keeps EG tails; kill can retain mixed-block/prefetch/filter output; panic clears pending output without allocation. Fixed 44.1 kHz synthesis is interpolated to 8–384 kHz mono output. Access is caller-serialized; no scheduler or portable snapshot is supplied. [MSFA details](research.md) describe the generated Native tree and each file |
| `wonderswan` | [MAME adaptation](../vendor/mame-wonderswan/README.md) / [WASM](../wasm/wonderswan_wasm.cpp) | The SDK Native target exposes the same raw C++ core used by the WASM bridge, without a Tauri wrapper. Four 32-point 4-bit waves, owned 16 KiB RAM, stereo levels, CH2 voice bytes, CH3 sweep and CH4 noise retain the preliminary MAME headphone model. Clock/output rate are fixed at construction; `floor(clock/128)` native ticks use integer-phase sample-and-hold output. Raw PCM is unipolar, sums unsigned contributions with `/1024` gain, and has no DC filter or normalization. Gate writes retain held PCM until a native tick; cold reset clears RAM, registers, mutes and held output. Mute masks output while synthesis advances. Unlike the Playground Web speaker adapter, this target does not center waveforms or add audition/clock/ownership management. The listening WAV host alone adds an explicit 20 Hz DC blocker, 0.7 gain and fades. No mono speaker, HyperVoice, DMA, CPU/ROM, system-volume gain, save-state or Playground Tauri Native Audio integration is provided. See the [Native guide](../native/README.md#embed-wonderswan) |

### Game Boy Native header amendment

The reference Web header originally lacked the following declaration from
Tauri's `src-tauri/native-gameboy/snapshot/third_party/mame-gameboy/gameboy_apu.h`.
The SDK now applies it inside `class GameboyApu` in the shared
[gameboy_apu.h](../vendor/mame-gameboy/gameboy_apu.h):

```cpp
friend struct NativeGameboyAccess; // Native state observation / gate-only Stop; DSP unchanged.
```

The Native wrapper uses it to observe and stop private counters/gates. It grants
access without changing layout, DSP, register semantics or the WASM API. The
vendor synthesis `.cpp`, Native `.cpp`/`.h` and WASM bridge remain byte-identical
to their imports. Source inventories retain the original Web header hash and
the amended SDK header hash rather than claiming a byte-identical header
import. The standalone target uses this same canonical vendor header; it does
not introduce a second core or redefine private access.

### NES / HuC6280 translation units

- NES: `vendor/tetorica-nes/nes_core.cpp` and `native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_nes.cpp` define the same `native_nes_*` symbols. The standalone `tetorica::nes` target compiles only the self-contained Native renderer; the WASM recipe uses the vendor implementation. Never add both translation units to one binary.
- HuC6280: the Native wrapper directly includes `huc6280.cpp`. Do not also add the vendor `.cpp` as another translation unit in that target. WASM uses the combination in its existing recipe.

## Existing upstream adaptations and inspection scope

This summary is based on the included README / UPSTREAM documents and current sources. Except where a MAME `upstream/` directory is retained, the SDK may not contain a complete unmodified upstream source tree. No project was fetched from the network for a full comparison against its latest version during this inspection.

| Chip or family | Existing Tetorica adaptations and limitations | Included evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ymfm chips | Observation, advancing feedback while muted, shared OPN frequency latches, dynamic OPL3 four-operator allocation, save / restore corrections and signed-shift fixes | [ymfm sources](../vendor/ymfm/), [source inventory](../catalog/source_inventory.json); see the historical comparison below |
| Sega PSG | Tetorica implementation covering tone / noise / stereo and host behavior | [segapsg.cpp](../vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/segapsg.cpp), [.h](../vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/segapsg.h) |
| Nuked-OPN2 | Uses kyorohiro fork `335747d78cb0abbc3b55b004e62dad9763140115`. The complete changes from nukeykt's original to this fork were not compared here | [README](../vendor/nuked-opn2/README.md); the included core matches both reference applications byte for byte |
| AY-3-8910 | Removes MAME device / CPU / stream infrastructure; retains an AY / YM2149 subset, averages three independent output tables and uses an integer-phase resampler. MAME's nonlinear single-pin mix and all chip variants are not implemented | [README](../vendor/mame-ay8910/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-ay8910/upstream/) |
| Game Boy | Ports the MAME DMG model to per-cycle ticks and an integrating resampler. Omits CGB / AGB, readback and the DMG wave-RAM corruption glitch | [README](../vendor/mame-gameboy/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-gameboy/upstream/) |
| HuC6280 | Makes six-channel wave / DDA / noise / LFO standalone; adds reset / mute / integer-phase averaging. Retains the original model's imperfect noise / LFO behavior | [README](../vendor/mame-huc6280/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-huc6280/upstream/) |
| WonderSwan | Adapts Wilbert Pol's pinned MAME sound device to byte-addressed I/O, owned 16 KiB RAM and integer-phase sample-and-hold output. Retains preliminary headphone behavior, unsigned DAC scaling, sweep/noise/voice semantics and documented hardware differences; adds deterministic cold reset and per-channel host mute. Removes device/CPU/stream/ROM dependencies; no mono speaker, DMA, HyperVoice or analog filter | [README](../vendor/mame-wonderswan/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-wonderswan/upstream/), [Native public forwarder](../native/include/tetorica/wonderswan.hpp) |
| RF5C164 | Exposes the 16-bit RF5C164 output with local 64 KiB RAM. Removes MAME CPU / device / sample-end callbacks; reset retains RAM | [README](../vendor/mame-rf5c164/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-rf5c164/upstream/) |
| OKIM6258 | Extracts the MAME decoder. Supports 4-bit ADPCM; 3-bit operation and recording are unavailable. Adds VGM pan / clock / divider and fractional hold | [README](../vendor/mame-okim6258/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-okim6258/upstream/) |
| 32X PWM | Extracts FIFO / timer / routing. Omits SH2 / DMA / video / analog PWM filtering; exposes interrupts as counts | [README](../vendor/mame-32x-pwm/README.md), [upstream originals](../vendor/mame-32x-pwm/upstream/), [core](../wasm/pwm32x_core.h) |
| NES + FDS | C++ port of the existing JSNES / fixNES adaptations, retaining the JavaScript int32 / rounding / nonlinear mix / filter / FDS behavior model | [README](../vendor/tetorica-nes/README.md), [JSNES origin](../vendor/tetorica-nes/UPSTREAM-JSNES.md), [FDS origin](../vendor/tetorica-nes/UPSTREAM-FDS.md); the complete original JavaScript sources are outside this SDK |
| SNES / SPC | Uses the accurate DSP with output mute, undefined-behavior fixes, 16-bit RAM wrap and trace / read-mask hooks. Does not use the fast DSP, optional filter, tempo control or surround-disable feature | [README](../vendor/snes-spc/README.md); the complete unmodified library and full Nintendo IPL ROM are not bundled |
| MSFA / DX7 | Standalone adaptation, initialized state, scalar selection, live controls and extreme-frequency arithmetic fixes, plus six Native overrides | [Details](research.md), [UPSTREAM](../vendor/msfa/UPSTREAM.md) |

The included ymfm sources were compared with Aaron Giles's commit `16e1d4281a59a60e589cf21f6b93329a8be5ff7a` (2024-09-06), retained in the reference repository's Git history. Its subject is `Use snprintf instead of sprintf to fix #59. Use std::array for operators to remove the need for array_size.` This establishes differences against that historical revision; it does not establish the current upstream version or its branch name at the time.

### YM2612 Nuked Native differences

The shared [nuked_opn2_wasm.c](../wasm/nuked_opn2_wasm.c) uses the existing adapter that advances 24 internal clocks × 11. The [Native wrapper](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_nuked.cpp) adds symbol prefixes and initial process-global chip-type configuration. [Additional YM2612 controls](../native/reference/tauri/native_genesis_nuked_ym2612.inc) provide source cancellation, Stop and output-rate averaging / hold. Only the include location changed during SDK import. The standalone `tetorica::nuked_ym2612` target exposes both retained synchronous raw `tetorica_nuked_*` and Native `native_nuked_ym2612_*` APIs. It compiles the core as C11 with supported private `-fwrapv` and eight per-source symbol prefixes and the wrapper as C++, linking platform threads for process-global one-time YM2612 selection. The wrapper/core bytes remain unchanged; see the [Native guide](../native/README.md#alternative-nuked-ym2612) for threading, DC, Stop/reset and buffer contracts.

## JavaScript-only Analyzer reference engines

| Reference | Origin and behavior | Native / WASM status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `msm5205` | [Engine](../reference/javascript/msm5205audioengine.js), imported unchanged from `web/msm5205audioengine.js`. The libvgm-derived model includes ADPCM decoding, a leaky accumulator, FIFO, reset, prescaler, 3/4-bit data, external VCLK, and fractional output timing. Mute masks output while decoder timing continues. [Original notices](../vendor/libvgm-msm5205/README.md) and [BSD license](../vendor/libvgm-msm5205/LICENSE) are retained | Not ported. The runnable JavaScript source is a behavioral reference; no CMake target or WASM recipe is claimed |
| `okim6295` | [Engine](../reference/javascript/okim6295audioengine.js), imported unchanged from `web/okim6295audioengine.js`. The MAME/libvgm-derived model has four ADPCM voices, sample-ROM command handling, clock/pin7 changes, standard and NMK112 banks, and held-sample output timing. Mute retains voice progression. [Original notices](../vendor/mame-okim6295/README.md) and [BSD license](../vendor/mame-okim6295/LICENSE) are retained | Not ported. The host supplies ROM data and event timing; the example generates synthetic data |

Both engines render stereo Float32 blocks synchronously and need no AudioContext. Their source comments retain the original repository paths for provenance; this SDK's relocated notices are linked above. The existing port notices did not pin their historical upstream revisions, so that limitation remains recorded with the exact Tetorica revision and hashes.

Separately collected source references now include libvgm's BSD-declared `msm5205.c`, `okim6295.c`, `okiadpcm.c` and `okiadpcm.h`, plus MAME's BSD-declared OKIM6295/ADPCM C++ files and headers. Each vendor snapshot records a full official commit and SHA-256 hashes. A newly collected revision does not establish the older JavaScript port's baseline.

These upstream C/C++ files are reference-only. MAME's framework is not bundled; libvgm integration headers and support/player code without explicit license declarations are omitted, with [the upstream licensing explanation](https://github.com/ValleyBell/libvgm/issues/129) linked in each component guide. The JavaScript engines and existing build targets do not depend on these omitted files. No game ROM is included.

See [reference/javascript/README.md](../reference/javascript/README.md) for the standalone example and APIs. These two references do not add Playground modes or `createSoundChip()` IDs.

## Licensing and future updates

Tetorica-authored SDK integration code and documentation use [BSD-3-Clause](../LICENSE), consistent with `tetorica-fm2612`, except where an existing explicit license applies. Third-party cores, adaptations with their own license and all existing copyright / license notices retain their terms. In particular, the six MSFA Native overrides retain Apache-2.0; Tetorica-authored wrapper headers without an individual declaration use the SDK's BSD-3-Clause default. [LICENSES.md](../LICENSES.md) maps the component terms.

When updating a chip, record the import version and hashes, upstream adaptations, import changes, Native-specific changes, required build combinations, API / Stop / sample-memory / output differences and verification scope. If variants are unified, record the revision and comparison results that established their equivalence.
